chunks: Jamil narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, regarding:

Regarding a muhrim who killed an ostrich, he عليه السلام said: “A camel is due upon him. If he cannot find one, then feeding sixty needy persons. If the value of the camel is greater than feeding sixty needy persons, he should not add beyond feeding sixty needy persons. And if the value of the camel is less than feeding sixty needy persons, then only the value of the camel is due upon him.”

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a camel offered as the required expiation
key_terms.سِتِّينَ: the specified number of needy persons to be fed
key_terms.قِيمَةُ: the monetary value used to determine the required amount
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.مِسْكِينًا: a needy person eligible to receive food in expiation
key_terms.نَعَامَةً: an ostrich hunted or killed while in ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for a muhrim who kills an ostrich in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a muhrim who kills an ostrich during ihram. The expiation is a camel, and if that is not available, feeding sixty needy people, with the liability capped or reduced according to the value of the camel. It reflects the structured fiqh of hunting violations in hajj and ihram.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2723 - Jamil narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding

a person in the state of ihram who killed an ostrich.
Imam (as) said: "They must offer a camel. If they cannot find one, they must feed sixty needy people. If the value of the camel exceeds the cost of feeding sixty needy people, they do not need to provide more than the feeding of sixty needy people. If the value of the camel is less than the cost of feeding sixty needy people, they are only required to pay the value of the camel."
